post.caption:
Sound is a compression wave: each bit of matter shoves its neighbour and the shove passes along, so nothing actually travels from the speaker to your ear except a pattern of pressure. Which means it needs a medium, and space is genuinely silent. Denser material passes the shove faster: around 340 m/s in air, roughly four times that in water, about fifteen times in steel. That is why whale calls cross oceans and why a rail tells you about the train early.
